value: Magistrate court (all counties except Bernalillo): either party may appeal to the district court of the county by filing a notice of appeal in district court within 15 days after the judgment is filed; the case is tried de novo (new trial) under Rule 1-072 NMRA. Bernalillo County Metropolitan Court: for ordinary civil cases (everything except landlord-tenant cases under the Uniform Owner-Resident Relations Act) Metro Court is a court of record, so the appeal goes to the New Mexico Court of Appeals on the record, by a notice of appeal filed in Metro Court within 30 days after the final order (Rule 3-706(C), effective for cases filed on or after Dec. 31, 2025; NMSA 34-8A-6(B)). Landlord-tenant (Owner-Resident Relations Act) judgments from Metro Court are appealed de novo to district court within 15 days (34-8A-6(C); Rule 3-706(B); Rule 1-072).

value: A claimant who starts a small claims case gives up the right to appeal, except that either party may appeal on the sole ground that substantial justice was not done between the parties under the rules of substantive law (CCA/UCCA/UDCA/UJCA 1807). Review is on the record (transcript or recording), not a new trial. Deadline: 30 days after service of the judgment with notice of entry (CPLR 5513(a)); in NYC Civil Court, 30 days from the earliest service of the judgment by the court or a party, plus 5 days if served by mail (CCA 1703(b)). Court: NYC Civil Court appeals go to the Appellate Term (CCA 1701); City, District and Town/Village Court appeals go to County Court unless the Appellate Division has directed them to the Appellate Term (UCCA, UDCA, UJCA 1701). A decision by a volunteer arbitrator (chosen instead of a judge) cannot be appealed, and a default judgment must first be challenged by a motion to vacate.

value: Small claims cases are usually heard by a magistrate. Either party may file written objections to the magistrate's decision within 14 days of its filing (another party may then object within 10 days after the first objections); objecting to findings of fact requires a transcript (Civ.R. 53(D)(3)(b)). The judge then rules and enters judgment. Either party may appeal the final judgment to the district court of appeals by filing a notice of appeal within 30 days of entry of the judgment (App.R. 4(A)); review is on the record, not a new trial. Failing to object to the magistrate's decision generally limits what can be raised on appeal.

value: Either party aggrieved by a magisterial district judge's money judgment may appeal within 30 days after the date of entry of the judgment by filing a notice of appeal (with a copy of the Notice of Judgment) with the prothonotary of the county Court of Common Pleas; late appeals only with leave of court for good cause (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 1002(A)). The appeal is a new trial (de novo) under the ordinary Common Pleas rules (Rule 1007(A)). Philadelphia Municipal Court money judgments are likewise appealed to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of entry on the docket, de novo (Phila. Civ. R. *1001 et seq.).
